transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um… I guess work thought I should come in. I’m an EMT, and there was kind of an incident at the station. I wasn’t trying to cause trouble or anything.

I was organizing the airway bags in the bay, just putting them in a pattern that felt… right, I guess. And I was saying some dispatch numbers out loud, repeating them. My lieutenant told me to stop and step away, but I had a hard time doing that because it felt like if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would… go bad somehow.

I know that probably sounds strange. I’m trying to explain it the right way.
Can you tell me more about what you meant when you said it had to feel 'right' and that the bay would 'go bad' if you broke the sequence?

Yeah… I mean, I know it sounds odd when I say it out loud. It wasn’t like I wanted to be difficult.

The airway bags were just… not in the right order, and I started moving them into a pattern that made sense to me. And the dispatch numbers—I was repeating them out loud because it felt like they sort of matched the pattern, or kept it steady. If I stopped before it was finished, it felt like the whole bay would be wrong… like something bad would happen there, or it would all go off somehow.

When my lieutenant told me to step away, I really did hear him, I wasn’t ignoring him on purpose. I just… couldn’t make myself break it right then. I thought if I did, the bay would go bad. Does that make sense, or am I explaining it badly?
Do you often feel like you have to complete certain actions or thoughts in a specific way to prevent something bad from happening, even if you know it might not make sense logically?

Yeah… I mean, I guess that’s what happened at the station. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but I did feel like I had to finish it a certain way.

I kept moving the airway bags into this pattern that I knew was right, and I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud. When my lieutenant told me to stop, I heard him, I did… I just couldn’t step away right then because it felt like if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would go bad somehow.

I know logically that probably doesn’t make sense. I’m not trying to be dramatic. It just felt really real in the moment. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Do you often have thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want or that bother you, and do you ever feel like you have to do something over and over again to make those thoughts go away or to keep something bad from happening?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m doing it all the time or trying to be difficult.

At the station, it was more like the thought got stuck that the airway bags had to be in the right pattern, and I kept repeating the dispatch numbers out loud because it felt like that kept things… steady, I guess. And when my lieutenant told me to stop, I heard him, I really did, but I couldn’t step away right then.

It felt like if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would go bad somehow. I know that probably sounds strange, but that’s what it felt like in the moment. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
